summary: Ryudo Fujii is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under Albrecht Wezler and Harunaga Isaacson. Fujii held posts at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 2003), Kokushikan University (attested 2010), and Kyoto Women's University (attested 2015).

Ryugen Taga (born 1931) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (~1953–1955). He spent his academic career at Rissho University as lecturer (~1958–1965), associate professor (~1965–1975), professor (~1975–2002), and president (~1992–1998).

Ryugen Tanemura (born 1970) specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. Tanemura held posts at Nishogakusha University (attested 2013), Kawasaki Daishi Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2014), and Taisho University (attested 2014–2018).

Ryuichi Abe (born 1954) specializes in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. Educated at Keio, SAIS/Johns Hopkins, and Columbia, he held posts at Columbia University (1991, 1998–2004) and Harvard University (~2006).
Ryukai Mano (1928–2015) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Succeeding Yuishin Ito, he served as a professor at Taisho University (attested 1991).

Ryuken Sato (1930–2018) worked in Buddhist studies. He held posts as professor emeritus at Taisho University (attested 2014) and advisor at the Kawasaki Daishi Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2014).
Ryusei Keira works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. Keira studied at the University of Lausanne under doctoral supervisor Tom Tillemans, completing a thesis by 2003.

Ryushin Uryuzu (1932–2015) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. After studying at Ryukoku University (~1950–1957), he held posts at the Tibetan Tripitaka Research Institute (attested 1962) and as professor at Kyoto Women's University (~1974–1998).
Ryusho Onami (born 1926) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Taishun Mibu. He held a post as a lecturer at Taisho University (attested 1985).
Ryuta Kikutani specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. Kikutani held posts at Tohoku University (attested 2015) and Kyoto University (attested 2020).

Ryutaro Tsuchida (born 1947) specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Tokyo and University of Marburg under Wilhelm Rau, he held positions at Marburg (~1977–1983) and the University of Tokyo (1983, 1995–2012).
Ryō Nishimura (1972–2016) worked in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He studied at Tohoku University (~1991–1995) and under Fumihiko Sueki (~1995–2004).
Ryōshū Matsushita (born 1944) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Daishun Ueyama. He held an appointment as lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 1987).

Ryūjō Yamada (1895–1979) specialized in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. After studying at Tokyo Imperial University and under Sylvain Lévi, he held posts at Ryukoku University (~1921–1944), Hōbōgirin (~1927–1930), Tohoku University (~1944–1979), and Musashino University (~1961–1968).

Ryūshō Hikata (1892–1991) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at the University of Tokyo under Junjirō Takakusu and Tohoku University. He held posts at Tokyo, Kyushu University (1940–1958), and Fukuoka Women's University (1960–1964).
Ryūzan Nishimoto was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Chishu Kitagawa and Chijo Kitagawa in 1916.
Ryūō Asahi (1856–1926) was a scholar in the field of Buddhist studies who held teaching posts at Tō-ji and Koyasan University.

Rüdiger Schmitt (born 1939) is a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied under Karl Hoffmann (~1960–1965) and held a post at Saarland University (~1972–2004).
S. A. S. Sarma is an Indology scholar who held posts at the École Française d'Extrême-Orient (attested 2004 and 2024).
S. Bhaskaran Nair worked in Indology and held posts at the Vishveshvaranand Vedic Research Institute, serving as General Editor (attested 1944, 1992) and Deputy Director (attested 1974–1977, 1986).
